name: aitp-control-plane
//aitp: SDK floors that are load-bearing for THIS service, each with its consequence if violated -- same convention as `//overrides` below: the rationale for a non-obvious version floor must live next to it or it will be lost. `0.5.0`: the JCS signing input moved from the transport wrapper to the inner artifact body for revocation snapshots (RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.1); aitp-rs implements no dual-accept, so a snapshot signed by <0.5.0 does not verify under >=0.5.0 and vice versa. This repo is the *issuer* of the revocation list, so under-floor here silently breaks every downstream verifier, and under a fail-closed revocation policy that surfaces as a spurious TCT_REVOKED -- an availability incident that reads like a network problem, not a version mismatch. `0.6.0`: `verifyRevocationList` exists at all -- `src/e2e/revocation-flow.integration.test.ts` requires it -- and ships with its typed `.code` contract; docs/api.md's advice to branch on `.code` is true from here. `0.7.0`: `verifyManifestJson` failures first carry a typed `.code`; `src/lib/registry/enrollment.ts:55` calls `verifyManifestJson` on externally-supplied input, and Phase 3 of this plan tightens the `.code`-is-a-string assertion on exactly that path. `0.11.0` (current): NOT a wire-shape floor for this repo -- its one BREAKING entry (the pinned-key proof timestamp erratum, RFC-AITP-0002 §3.1) is unreachable here because this service exposes no handshake endpoint. Recorded explicitly so a future reader does not have to re-derive that. Caret trap: on a 0.x range npm's `^` pins the minor, so `^0.10.0` never resolves `0.11.0` and no `npm update` moves it -- only a deliberate range edit (or the bump-aitp workflow) does.
//overrides: Transitive security floor for `npx audit-ci --config ./audit-ci.jsonc` (the CI gate: prod deps, high+). The postcss and sharp floors that used to live here are GONE as of the next 16.3.2 upgrade (#47): they existed only because next 15.5.x hard-pinned postcss 8.4.31 and shipped sharp ^0.34.3, and next 16.3.x ships the fixed versions natively -- which was always the stated removal condition. brace-expansion is a SEPARATE chain (@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node -> resource-detector-gcp -> gcp-metadata -> gaxios -> rimraf -> glob -> minimatch@9), unrelated to next, and is deliberately SCOPED, not global: this tree legitimately resolves three majors of brace-expansion -- minimatch@10 (top level, used by eslint) needs ^5.0.5, minimatch@9 needs ^2.0.2, minimatch@3 needs ^1.1.7 -- and a global pin to 2.x breaks eslint with `TypeError: (0 , brace_expansion_1.expand) is not a function`, because only 5.x exports a named `expand`. Remove this entry when @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node stops resolving a vulnerable brace-expansion.
